The user says "午休时间到了" (Lunch break time has arrived) and explicitly says not to call any tools, not to read files, just answer directly.

This is a simple conversational turn. I should just respond naturally. No tools. Keep it brief and friendly, respecting the constraint. Maybe note I won't do anything, wish them a good break, and note that if they want to pick up the todo list or screenshots later, I'm here.

I should keep it short — it's a lunch break. Don't dump a huge list. Maybe one short paragraph with a light offer for after the break. Avoid repeating the BETA/dark theme/cat disclaimers unnecessarily — that would be annoying. Though the prior pattern included them; but here it's just lunch. Keep it human.
